title: POC Weekly Sync — Reliability incident follow-up

transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-20
Time: 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~42 minutes
Attendees: Jamie Park (Redwood AE), Samir Patel (Redwood SE), Maya Alvarez (Astra Eng Mgr), Tom Reeves (Astra SRE), Nina Rao (Astra Product), Leo Kim (Astra Dev), Olga Petrova (Astra Security)

Summary (auto): Quick sync to follow up on last week's reliability incident — intermittent timeouts, increased 5xx rate during traffic spike, some evidence of client-side retry storms and upstream rate-limits. Discussed mitigation and next steps.

00:00 Jamie (Redwood AE): All right, thanks everybody for joining, we'll keep this tight, 30, 45 minutes, going to run through the incident timeline and then Samir will share what we've found on the SE side. Maya, Tom, anything immediate before we jump in?
00:28 Maya (Astra): No, just that the spike hit our weekend load test, it caused a few customer-facing errors. We had some pages show 504s and timeouts to downstream endpoints.
00:40 Tom (Astra): Yeah, to add, we saw a surge of retries from our client app, that made things worse, so we want to understand if Redwood is doing any throttling or if the 5xxs came from the model infra.
01:05 Samir (Redwood SE): Thanks. Quick caveat, I'm going to read a couple things off the logs, transcripts have minor OCR like, um, known issues — so if any name is off, say so. We correlated request-ids you sent: we see a cluster of 502/504 responses between 02:12 and 02:35 UTC on 2026-03-18. Those align with a traffic ramp where concurrent open sessions jumped ~3x.
01:35 Samir: Initial root-cause hypothesis is multi-factor: (1) client-side aggressive retries w/o exponential backoff, (2) upstream rate-limits at our partner edge, (3) KV cache churn causing cold-kv loads for the same prefixes. The combination produced higher tail latency.
02:05 Tom: When you say "KV cache" in the logs it sometimes comes across as "K V cash" in the transcript, so yes, we suspect cache thrash — we saw cache hit rate drop from 92% to 58% during the spike.
02:30 Jamie: Did we observe any GPU OOMs or model-level errors?
02:35 Samir: No OOMs. The model processes were healthy; CPU/GPU metrics stayed within expected bounds. The 5xxs are mostly gateway 502/504 from the routing tier when queueing throttled requests.
03:00 Nina (Astra): Also to add, some of our routes are larger payloads with longer generation windows, those got queued so subsequent short calls were delayed.
03:18 Samir: Right — we saw longer seq length requests monopolizing concurrency due to lack of per-route limits. That's one short-term fix we recommended: per-route concurrency caps + more aggressive request shedding for very long sequences.
03:40 Maya: Can you walk through retries? Our app uses a retry of 3 with fixed backoff 1s, which I think is a problem.
03:50 Samir: Fixed backoff is dangerous in spikes. We suggest moving to exponential backoff with jitter, starting 200ms, max 4s, and limit total retries to 2 for idempotent calls. Also add a client-side circuit breaker when error rate exceeds threshold.
04:15 Tom: Any advice on rate limits? We hit a 429 band at the edge for some tokens.
04:24 Samir: There were two layers — our edge rate limiter and an upstream partner queue. In some cases, the edge returned a 429 which your client retried, causing more load. If you can surface 429s to user-logic (i.e., don't automatically retry 429s except after a backoff), that helps.
04:45 Olga (Astra Security): On the security side, were there any anomalous auth failures?
04:50 Samir: No, all auth checks passed; keys valid. No suspicious traffic.
05:12 Jamie: Quick status — Redwood is proposing two tracks: immediate mitigations (retry/backoff change, per-route caps, short-term burst capacity), and a longer-term ops runbook + replay benchmark to reproduce.
05:30 Maya: That sounds good. Can you explain the burst capacity option? Is that Redwood Dedicated only?
05:40 Jamie: Burst is available both on Dedicated and on Hosted as a configured burst pool — Dedicated gives stronger isolation and guaranteed throughput but requires commit. For the POC we can enable temporary burst capacity for the test cluster to avoid queueing while we tune. I'll send pricing.
06:05 Leo (Astra Dev): Samir, do you have example backoff configs we can copy?
06:12 Samir: Yes, I'll include a sample. Roughly: initial=200ms, multiplier=2.0 with full jitter, max=4s, maxAttempts=2 for user-visible endpoints. For internal background jobs you can be more aggressive.
06:35 Jamie: Let's go into the specific incident timeline and logs — Samir?
06:42 Samir: Sure. I have an example set — request-id 8f7b6a contained a 504 at 02:18 UTC. We traced it through the router -> inference pool -> partner queue where we saw a backlog. The router's queue length spiked to 1200 for 30s.
07:05 Tom: That's consistent with what we measured. We also saw a spike in socket timeouts on our side.
07:18 Samir: One nuance — some clients were sending batched requests incorrectly; a few SDK versions sent large multi-turn payloads in a single request which increased compute per call. Versioning issue, we flagged that in the doc.
07:45 Maya: Which SDK versions? We need to patch them.
07:50 Samir: The telemetry shows v1.4.2 in ~12% of calls. It packs multiple conversations into one payload. Recommend pinning to 1.4.0 or later patch, we'll provide guidance.
08:10 Nina: Do we have a split of 5xx by route/model?
08:15 Samir: Yes — I'll attach a CSV. Most errors concentrated on the 'summarize-long' route with seq-length > 800 tokens.
08:28 Jamie: On monitoring and alerting — Samir, can you propose thresholds?
08:33 Samir: Baseline: p95 latency < 600ms for short routes, 5xx rate < 0.5% sustained. Alert on sudden 5xx increase > 0.5% within 5 minutes or queue length > 500. We'll include sample PromQLs in the runbook.
09:00 Tom: Are those alerts supported in Redwood Console?
09:05 Jamie: Yes, Redwood Console supports per-route alerting and tracing hooks. We can add integrations with your PagerDuty.
09:18 Maya: On the replay benchmark — what does Redwood need from us?
09:24 Samir: We need representative payload samples, request-ids (already requested), and a list of routes and seq-length distribution. Then we'll run replays against a staging cluster with the same concurrency to reproduce tail behavior.
09:40 Maya: We'll pack that and share today.
10:02 Tom: One additional concern — we occasionally see spikes of 5xx when we hit tokenization boundary, any quick wins there?
10:12 Samir: Tokenization boundary causing longer runtimes is expected; quick win is to enforce server-side token limits on route or remote reject very-long requests with a clear 4xx so clients don't retry. Also marking non-idempotent long calls as low-priority to shed load.
10:35 Nina: From product POV, we want to avoid user-visible errors. Can Redwood do transparent retries on our behalf?
10:42 Jamie: We can do transparent retries at the edge but it's risky — it can mask retries and aggravate load. We prefer client-side backoff unless you use a circuit-breaker pattern. For important short calls, we can configure fast-paths.
11:05 Maya: How fast can we get the temp burst enabled? We have another load test Wed.
11:12 Jamie: We can enable burst for the POC cluster within 24-48 hours, I will coordinate with ops. Pricing note will be in the follow-up.
11:30 Samir: Quick note about logs: please include the full request-id header and the timing frames, that makes correlation much faster.
11:45 Tom: Will do.
12:00 Jamie: We're ~12 minutes in, let's hit remaining items — escalate any security questions?
12:10 Olga: No immediate ones, but we'll want the log retention and access control details.
12:18 Jamie: I'll attach the SOC2 and retention policy doc in the follow-up.
12:30 Samir: One more technical suggestion — enable per-route KV cache warming for high-impact prefixes so cold-cache churn doesn't blow up latency during spikes.
12:48 Maya: Okay that seems plausible.
13:00 Jamie: Let's do a quick recap and action items. Samir, you said you'll share logs and a draft runbook — timeline?
13:10 Samir: I'll share initial logs + sample configs by Monday (2026-03-22) and runbook draft by Friday (2026-03-26).
13:25 Jamie: Maya/Tom to run the replay harness and share payloads by Wednesday (2026-03-25)?
13:32 Maya: Yes, we'll prioritize that.
13:40 Jamie: I'll send a calendar invite for the ops deep-dive Tue 2026-03-23 and include proposed agenda: replay results, retry/backoff, per-route caps, runbook.
13:52 Nina: Good. Any blockers on Redwood side for the replay?
13:56 Samir: None — just the payloads and request-ids. We'll also try a controlled burst run.
14:10 Jamie: Anything else from anyone?
14:18 Tom: Not from me, thanks for the clear next steps.
14:25 Maya: Thanks.
14:35 Jamie: Great, we'll follow up with the items discussed. Meeting adjourned.
